chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Abi al-Mi'za, from Abi Basir, who said:
I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A man exited his ihram, while his wife had not yet exited hers, and he had intercourse with her. He said: Upon her is a badanah, which her husband must pay for.

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: his state of ihram for pilgrimage rites
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a sacrificial camel or large animal due as expiation
key_terms.يَغْرَمُهَا: he must bear its cost or pay for it

ai.seo_question: If a husband leaves ihram but his wife has not, and he has intercourse with her, what expiation is required?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a husband who has exited the ihram of mut'ah while his wife has not yet exited hers, and he has intercourse with her. The ruling states that a badanah is due on her behalf, and the husband is liable to pay it.
